subject.title: [security] WebVNC and Code agent tickets can be consumed after GitHub revocation

question: Should WebVNC and Code backend bridge tickets fail closed at consumption time when the GitHub bridge grant that minted them is no longer current?
rationale: The source evidence supports the security gap, but the repair changes coordinator credential storage and authorization semantics in a security boundary that should receive maintainer/security acceptance.

options.title: Mirror egress revocation
options.body: Store bridge-grant context for WebVNC and Code tickets and reject stale GitHub grants at consumption time, matching the documented egress behavior.

options.title: Accept the short window
options.body: Document that WebVNC and Code backend tickets may remain valid for their 120-second TTL after GitHub revocation.

options.title: Redesign bridge tickets
options.body: Pause the narrow fix and do a broader bridge-ticket credential model pass across WebVNC, Code, egress, and future bridge classes.

recommendation.title: Mirror egress revocation
recommendation.body: Store bridge-grant context for WebVNC and Code tickets and reject stale GitHub grants at consumption time, matching the documented egress behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history in the Worker bridge-auth and revocation code now under review.
